subject: music
title: Set-Work Analysis Vocabulary III
meta_desc: A-Level Music: vocabulary for form and performance practice.

concepts.def: Same music repeated for each verse of text.
The most-used range of a voice or instrument in a piece.
The basso-continuo group — bass instrument plus keyboard.

walkthroughs.body_html: Strophic songs use one melody for all verses (hymns, folk songs). Through-composed songs evolve continuously, music responding to text (Schubert's Erlkönig, 1815).
Tessitura describes where a singer spends most time, not absolute range. Coloratura writing (Mozart's Queen of the Night, 1791) demands rapid agility in the high register.
Vocabulary about ensemble: a cappella = voices alone; continuo = the bass-plus-keyboard group of Baroque practice. Mention performing forces in every answer.

mcqs.q: Same music for each verse is:

options: Continuous bass line, ornamentation, terraced dynamics, and counterpoint.
A single melody with chord accompaniment.
Two or more independent melodic lines sounding together.
